proof_points.evidence: A ~$100M, ~100-vessel foiling network is ramping in the Maldives on the identical resort-transfer pattern.
proof_points.source: Navier x JIH Global, WSJ May 2026

objections.concern: Bolt competes mainly on price in Egypt.
objections.response: Hydrofoiling is ~10x more efficient than a planing boat, so the economics work at scale — and the water tier is a differentiated product Bolt can own where price-only competition is fiercest on land.

objections.concern: The Gulf of Suez crossing is exposed.
objections.response: Quanta-LR (700 nm hybrid) is built for the cross-gulf line-haul; Pioneer II serves the sheltered intra-Riviera and reef hops.

objections.concern: Bolt is a recent entrant with no marine experience in Egypt.
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal and the existing licensed dive-and-transfer fleets provide the regulatory path — Bolt supplies demand and the app; Navier supplies the fleet and ops model.

phases.rationale: The densest Red Sea resort cluster and a differentiated product for Bolt's scaling Egyptian base.

phases.rationale: Marquee dive destinations where zero-wake foiling is an environmental differentiator.

phases.rationale: A long cross-gulf corridor served today only by ferry or flight — the natural Quanta-LR showcase.

end_state.headline: Bolt's in-app water layer on Egypt's Red Sea Riviera.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Hurghada + El Gouna + Sahl Hasheesh + Sharm el-Sheikh + Marsa Alam — Egypt's Red Sea resort-and-reef coast, on Bolt's fast-scaling Egyptian demand base.
end_state.narrative: Starting from the Hurghada/El Gouna Riviera, Bolt and Navier make Egypt's Red Sea a differentiated in-app water surface: silent reef and resort transfers replacing the diesel day-boat fleet, premium dive runs at Sharm and Marsa Alam, and a Quanta-LR cross-gulf line-haul — an ownable product on the coast Bolt is racing to capture on land.

close.title: Egypt's Red Sea, the Bolt way.
close.body: The Hurghada Riviera first, then Sharm and Marsa Alam and the cross-gulf line-haul — Bolt's differentiated water layer on Egypt's Red Sea, foiling and in-app.

markets.corridors_note: From a Hurghada↔El Gouna hop to Sharm reef runs and a Quanta-LR cross-gulf line-haul.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance & certification path, and a uniform integration spec.
the_ask.partner_brings: Demand, the rider/guest relationship, and Egypt — Cairo & the Red Sea as the launch market to prove the on-water tier.
the_ask.next_step: Scope a Phase-1 pilot (~5 vessels) on the entry corridor, building to ~106 vessels as the network matures (addressable ceiling ~264).

objections.concern: Ground ride-hail is our core — why move onto water?
objections.response: Water is the one urban surface Bolt's mission of cheaper, cleaner, car-free mobility hasn't reached. Across the Saronic, the Dalmatian coast and the Gulf, the sea is the fastest line between two points — and no super-app owns it yet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough for the Mediterranean and Gulf?
objections.response: Most coastal and island hops are short — inside the all-electric Pioneer II's 70 nm envelope. The Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer island and cross-gulf legs up to 700 nm with no charging infrastructure required.

objections.concern: We operate in 45+ countries — how do we launch without huge overhead?
objections.response: You don't build or run the fleet. Navier brings vessels, captains and maintenance; Bolt brings demand, dispatch, the wallet and the brand. Each coastal city is a self-contained pilot on existing berths — no new infrastructure.

objections.concern: Will a water tier fit Bolt's value positioning?
objections.response: Foiling's low energy per passenger-mile is exactly what makes an affordable water option viable. It's cleaner and car-free — on-brand for Bolt — and the resort corridors fund the launch while commuters get a faster crossing.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: Anchor: $15M/yr of premium sea-transfer spend on the sourced corridors today. Every rung is a transformation of that one grounded number.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.
